title: How to Balance Light in the Camera

cards.prompt: What is exposure in photography, and which three parameters make it up?
cards.answer: Exposure is the amount of light hitting the camera sensor; it consists of ISO, shutter speed, and aperture.

cards.prompt: Aperture is how wide the lens opens; the larger the opening, the ____ light it captures.
What is the trade-off of raising the ISO?
cards.answer: Higher ISO makes the camera more sensitive to light in dim scenes, but adds more noise.
How long the camera spends capturing the photo (how long light is let in).

cards.prompt: You are shooting in a bright park at noon and your photo comes out washed out. Which ISO setting direction suits this well-lit scene?
cards.answer: Use a low ISO: it is less sensitive to light, which suits well-lit environments and gives less noise.

cards.prompt: Which one is NOT part of the exposure settings?
cards.answer: Tripod height is unrelated; ISO, shutter speed, and aperture make up exposure.
